title: Sustainable biodiesel synthesis: Valorization of waste materials as heterogeneous catalysts
content:
Abstract

Recently, research efforts have intensified to develop biodiesel production techniques that are both cost-effective and environmentally responsible, driven by the growing demand for sustainable alternatives to fossil fuels. This study investigates the potential of waste-derived heterogeneous catalysts supported on Iranian clinoptilolite for biodiesel synthesis from waste cooking oil. The novelty of this work lies in the fabrication of CaO-rich catalysts from locally available waste materials (construction lime, mussel shell, and kettle limescale) supported on natural clinoptilolite and the systematic optimization of acetone-assisted transesterification using Box–Behnken design. The transesterification process was optimized by varying catalyst concentration, methanol-to-oil ratio, and solvent-to-oil ratio at a constant temperature of 60°C and a reaction time of 120 min. The synthesized catalysts were characterized using XRD, FT-IR, and SEM techniques. The results revealed that identical optimum conditions (8 wt% catalyst, methanol-to-oil ratio of 0.7 v/v, and solvent-to-oil ratio of 0.4 v/v) were obtained for all three catalysts. Among them, the kettle limescale/clinoptilolite catalyst achieved the highest biodiesel conversion of 98.75%. These findings demonstrate that waste-derived clinoptilolite-supported catalysts provide a sustainable, low-cost, and efficient alternative for biodiesel production while promoting waste valorization and circular economy principles.
